capabilities: Built-in inference lowering appends checked descriptors to one shared vector. Old custom inference_ops implementations retain a default append bridge.
Sequential restores the caller prefix after a child error; leaf validation and descriptor order, parameter handles, shapes and layouts are unchanged.

The cache uses revocable weak content witnesses for unchanged native values. External or foreign sources retain per-element exact comparison. Equal-value replacement can refresh its witness without recompilation.

TensorContentStamp never retains values or forces a value-sized COW copy. A successful shared mutable DLPack export revokes existing stamps through all outer aliases; copy-only and failed exports do not.
Parameter finite validation caches positive results only for tracked values. CPU packed weights are rebuilt for untracked sources, repairing the late-export stale-pack regression.
Dedicated native allocation tests compare the former Vec-per-leaf assembly with the same current checked leaf descriptors; production allocator and GPU timing are not instrumented.
Existing direct graph I/O, stage guards, output slots and GPU arithmetic are unchanged. Original Module calls inherit the CPU preparation changes in Rust, Python and WASM.
boundaries: Reuse is ownership-gated, not a claim of global allocation-free execution. Per-call descriptors, CPU parameter checks, command encoders, an upstream guard copy, final guard pass and terminal readbacks remain.
The 32 MiB budget is retained output values/flags, not total physical GPU, binding, model or scratch memory. User-retained outputs can exceed it.

No GPU arithmetic, shader, guard-addressing, queue schedule, error threshold or automatic pure Tensor/autograd/ModuleTrainer routing changes. Finite parameter validation remains strict; unchanged tracked parameters reuse its positive result.
Browser A/B uses separate WASM/device instances in one page with rotated serial routes. Physical browser GPU and host exclusivity UNKNOWN; browser samples are visibly quantized.
The timed explicit graph and eager Torch implementations are unchanged controls in this slice. All route ratios remain descriptive, without normalization that hides drift.
Native versions run serially in separate processes, each with eager Torch controls. Control drift is retained and cannot be entirely attributed to the code change.
Burst means eight independent fixed-input forwards plus final completed host observation, not recurrent decoding, peak GPU timestamps or fastest PyTorch.
No CUDA/Furnace, push, merge or release in this slice. Both clients are rebuilt from the selected main-worktree source. The baseline is the immediately preceding verified assembly-only runtime.
selection_context: Source-bound comparison against immediately preceding assembly-only 91b8b4c7. No parameter transfer, arithmetic or shader optimization is bundled. Development compiler failures and the reproduced stale-pack failure remain archived separately from adopted verification.
